neighbours.label: something made contingent on what happens to be available or arise ('subject to availability', 'whatever is available', 'as needs arise', 'what the market will bear')
fire: Rooms with a sea view are given out subject to availability at check-in.
The soup changes daily, made from whatever is available in the garden.
Extra staff are brought in as needs arise over the holidays.
Landlords here charge whatever the market will bear.
In my notebook I sketch whatever comes into my mind on the train.
Places on the course are limited and offered subject to capacity.
We slept wherever the road happened to take us that summer.
The clinic uses whichever vaccine is available in the region at the time.
quiet: Rooms with a sea view are given out to families at check-in.
The soup changes daily, made from leeks and potatoes in the kitchen.
Extra staff are brought in by bus over the holidays.
Landlords here charge six hundred pounds a month.
In my notebook I sketch the other passengers on the train.
Places on the course are free and offered to local students.
We slept in a small tent by the lake that summer.
The clinic uses a single vaccine made in the region by one firm.

notes: Top examples: 'whatever else pops into my brain', 'subject to enrolment capacity', 'as needs rise', 'what the market will bear', 'wherever the milky way ran'; output direction promotes ' available', ' dictated', ' determined', ' whenever'. Probes: 'what the market will bear' 0.70, 'whatever is available' 0.54, 'subject to availability' 0.40, 'as needs arise' 0.36, 'whatever pops into my head' 0.34; plain controls 0.00-0.01.
